page: Amazon Web Services dl2q.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered primarily for deep learning inference workloads. The hardware profile is driven by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor offering 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 35 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, BMI2, and FMA. For memory capacity, the host integrates 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by eight Qualcomm AI100 inference accelerators offering a total of 125 GB of VRAM. The system is provisioned without local instance storage and depends on network-attached storage, supported by a 100 Gbps baseline network interface under the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate distinct performance characteristics across execution paradigms. Highly parallel multi-threaded workloads score within the top 25%, as reflected by a stress-ng multi-core result of 81310.77, a PassMark CPU score of 55760.63, and strong throughput in CPU encryption (37139.12) and extended instructions (74264.06). Memory subsystems maintain strong bandwidth for cached operations (4504.08 GB/sec in small-block reads) and 220.46 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, contributing to high throughput in in-memory operations like Redis SET commands (75.32 million ops/sec) and static web serving (45.89 GB/sec). Conversely, single-core metrics fall into lower tiers; stress-ng single-core (1370.79) and single-threaded gzip compression (23.46 GB/sec) test in the bottom 25%, while Geekbench single-core sits in the middle 50% at 1257.0.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on high aggregate parallel scale versus constrained single-thread execution speed and the absence of ephemeral local NVMe drives. While traditional GPU tasks often lean on NVIDIA CUDA stacks, the Qualcomm AI100 architecture targets power-conscious, high-density inference throughput. The dl2q.24xlarge instance provides strong resource density across its 96 vCPUs, 768 GB RAM, 100 Gbps network pipe, and 8 specialized ASIC accelerators, making it suitable for distributed deep learning inference, high-concurrency model serving pipelines, real-time image processing, and parallel data transformation pipelines where local drive caching is not required.
description: Amazon Web Services dl2q.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance optimized for machine learning inference. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor, it provides 48 physical cores, 96 dedicated vCPUs at 2.5 GHz, and 768.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. Acceleration is driven by eight Qualcomm AI100 inference processors totaling 125 GB of VRAM. The system lacks local instance storage but provides a 100 Gbps baseline network connection through the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Benchmark data reflects top-tier multi-threaded CPU throughput, strong extended instruction performance, and substantial memory read bandwidth, paired with weaker single-core processing capabilities. With its high vCPU-to-memory density and dedicated inference accelerators, the dl2q.24xlarge is engineered for large-scale model inference, parallel deep learning tasks, and high-throughput data serving.
